sections.title: Complete Beginner's Guide to 7 Advanced Features
sections.body:
You already know:
✅ Nodes, Edges, StateGraph  
✅ Conditional Edges  
✅ Fan-in / Fan-out  
✅ Loops  
✅ Tool Calling & ToolNode  
✅ Human-in-the-Loop  
✅ Short-term & Long-term Memory  
✅ Reducers  

This notebook covers everything **else** that matters:

| Part | Topic | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **MessagesState** — built-in chat state | 3 |
| 2 | **Subgraphs** — graph inside a graph | 3 |
| 3 | **Multi-Agent / Supervisor** — team of AI agents | 3 |
| 4 | **Streaming** — see output live | 3 |
| 5 | **Time Travel** — replay & fork history | 3 |
| 6 | **`create_react_agent`** — instant ReAct agent | 3 |
| 7 | **Send API** — dynamic map-reduce | 3 |

```

```

sections.title: Setup — Run This First!
sections.body:
```python
import operator, asyncio, json
from typing import Annotated, TypedDict, List, Literal, Optional

# LangGraph core
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END, MessagesState
from langgraph.graph.message import add_messages
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver
from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode, tools_condition, create_react_agent
from langgraph.types import Send, interrupt, Command

# LangChain
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, AIMessage, SystemMessage, ToolMessage
from langchain_core.tools import tool

# Groq LLM
from langchain_groq import ChatGroq
from IPython.display import Image, display

GROQ_API_KEY = "<REDACTED_API_KEY>"
MODEL        = "openai/gpt-oss-20b"
llm = ChatGroq(api_key=GROQ_API_KEY, model=MODEL, temperature=0.3)

print("✅ Setup complete! LLM ready →", MODEL)
```

sections.title: What is MessagesState?
sections.body:
`MessagesState` is a **prebuilt TypedDict** that LangGraph ships with.
Instead of writing `messages: Annotated[list, add_messages]` every time,
you can just inherit from `MessagesState` and it's done for you.

```python
# The LONG way (what you did before):
class MyState(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[list, add_messages]
    name: str

# The SHORT way with MessagesState:
class MyState(MessagesState):   # ← inherits messages field automatically!
    name: str                   # just add your extra fields
```

MessagesState gives you ONE field for free:
- `messages: Annotated[list, add_messages]` — full chat history with smart dedup

> Think of it as the "starter kit" state that every chatbot uses.

sections.title: Example 1 — Basic MessagesState Chatbot
sections.body:
**Simplest possible chatbot using MessagesState. No extra fields needed.**

```python
# MessagesState already has: messages: Annotated[list, add_messages]
# That's all a basic chatbot needs!

class BasicBotState(MessagesState):
    pass   # nothing extra needed — messages field is already included!

def bot_node(state: BasicBotState):
    # state["messages"] is the full conversation history
    reply = llm.invoke(state["messages"])
    return {"messages": [reply]}   # add_messages appends, not overwrites

g = StateGraph(BasicBotState)
g.add_node("bot", bot_node)
g.add_edge(START, "bot")
g.add_edge("bot", END)
app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "ms-demo-1"}}

print("=== Simple MessagesState Chatbot ===")
turns = [
    "Hi! I'm learning LangGraph.",
    "What am I learning?",     # tests memory
]
for user_msg in turns:
    r = app.invoke({"messages": [HumanMessage(user_msg)]}, config=cfg)
    print(f"You: {user_msg}")
    print(f"Bot: {r['messages'][-1].content[:150]}")
    print(f"  (total messages in history: {len(r['messages'])})")
    print()

print("✅ MessagesState handles the messages reducer automatically!")
```

sections.title: Example 2 — MessagesState + Extra Fields
sections.body:
**Add your own fields on top of the built-in messages field.**

```python
# Extend MessagesState with your own fields
class SupportState(MessagesState):
    ticket_id : str    # your custom field
    priority  : str    # your custom field
    resolved  : bool   # your custom field

def triage_node(state: SupportState):
    # Check the last human message to determine priority
    last_msg = state["messages"][-1].content.lower()
    if any(w in last_msg for w in ["urgent", "broken", "crash", "down"]):
        priority = "HIGH"
    elif any(w in last_msg for w in ["slow", "error", "bug"]):
        priority = "MEDIUM"
    else:
        priority = "LOW"
    print(f"  [triage] ticket {state['ticket_id']} → priority: {priority}")
    return {"priority": priority}

def support_agent_node(state: SupportState):
    system = SystemMessage(
        f"You are a support agent. Ticket #{state['ticket_id']}. "
        f"Priority: {state['priority']}. Reply in 1-2 sentences."
    )
    reply = llm.invoke([system] + state["messages"])
    # Mark as resolved for demo
    return {"messages": [reply], "resolved": True}

g = StateGraph(SupportState)
g.add_node("triage",  triage_node)
g.add_node("support", support_agent_node)
g.add_edge(START,     "triage")
g.add_edge("triage",  "support")
g.add_edge("support", END)
app = g.compile()

result = app.invoke({
    "messages"  : [HumanMessage("My app crashed and I can't log in — URGENT!")],
    "ticket_id" : "TKT-4821",
    "priority"  : "LOW",
    "resolved"  : False,
})
print(f"Ticket   : {result['ticket_id']}")
print(f"Priority : {result['priority']}")
print(f"Resolved : {result['resolved']}")
print(f"Reply    : {result['messages'][-1].content[:200]}")
print()
print("✅ MessagesState extended with ticket_id, priority, resolved fields!")
```

sections.title: Example 3 — MessagesState with System Prompt Injection
sections.body:
**Real pattern: inject a system prompt that controls the bot's personality.**

```python
class PersonaState(MessagesState):
    persona: str   # "teacher", "coach", or "friend"

PERSONAS = {
    "teacher": "You are a patient Python teacher. Explain clearly with examples. Keep it under 80 words.",
    "coach"  : "You are a motivational coding coach. Be encouraging and action-oriented. Under 60 words.",
    "friend" : "You are a friendly coding buddy. Be casual, fun, and helpful. Under 60 words.",
}

def persona_bot(state: PersonaState):
    persona_prompt = PERSONAS.get(state["persona"], PERSONAS["teacher"])
    system = SystemMessage(persona_prompt)
    reply  = llm.invoke([system] + state["messages"])
    return {"messages": [reply]}

g = StateGraph(PersonaState)
g.add_node("bot", persona_bot)
g.add_edge(START, "bot")
g.add_edge("bot", END)
app = g.compile()

question = "How do I understand Python decorators?"
print(f"Question: {question}\n")

for persona_name in ["teacher", "coach", "friend"]:
    r = app.invoke({
        "messages": [HumanMessage(question)],
        "persona" : persona_name,
    })
    print(f"[{persona_name.upper()}]")
    print(r["messages"][-1].content[:200])
    print()

print("✅ MessagesState + persona field = same graph, different personalities!")
```

sections.title: What is a Subgraph?
sections.body:
A **subgraph** is a compiled LangGraph graph used as a **node** inside another graph.

```
Main Graph:
  START → [preprocess_node] → [SUBGRAPH NODE] → [output_node] → END
                                      │
                              ┌───────▼────────┐
                              │   Sub-Graph    │
                              │  step1 → step2 │
                              │  → step3 → END │
                              └────────────────┘
```

### Why use subgraphs?
- **Modularity** — build complex pipelines from reusable pieces
- **Clarity** — each subgraph has a clear single responsibility
- **Reuse** — the same subgraph can be used in multiple parent graphs

### How to use a subgraph as a node:
```python
subgraph_app = sub_graph.compile()         # compile the sub-graph

main_graph.add_node("my_sub", subgraph_app)   # use it as a node!
```

> ⚠️ **Important:** The subgraph's state keys that you want to share with the
> parent graph must use the **same key names**.

sections.title: Example 4 — Text Cleaning Subgraph
sections.body:
**A subgraph that cleans text (strip → lowercase → remove punctuation) embedded in a main analysis pipeline.**

```python
import re

# ── SUB-GRAPH: Text Cleaner ─────────────────────────────────────
class CleanState(TypedDict):
    text: str   # shared key with parent

def strip_whitespace(state: CleanState):
    cleaned = state["text"].strip()
    print(f"  [sub: strip]     '{cleaned[:40]}'")
    return {"text": cleaned}

def to_lowercase(state: CleanState):
    cleaned = state["text"].lower()
    print(f"  [sub: lowercase] '{cleaned[:40]}'")
    return {"text": cleaned}

def remove_punctuation(state: CleanState):
    cleaned = re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", "", state["text"])
    print(f"  [sub: clean_punc] '{cleaned[:40]}'")
    return {"text": cleaned}

sub = StateGraph(CleanState)
sub.add_node("strip",  strip_whitespace)
sub.add_node("lower",  to_lowercase)
sub.add_node("clean",  remove_punctuation)
sub.add_edge(START, "strip")
sub.add_edge("strip", "lower")
sub.add_edge("lower", "clean")
sub.add_edge("clean", END)
text_cleaner = sub.compile()   # compiled subgraph = usable as a node

# ── PARENT GRAPH: Analysis Pipeline ────────────────────────────
class PipelineState(TypedDict):
    text      : str    # same key as subgraph → values flow through!
    word_count: int
    summary   : str

def count_words(state: PipelineState):
    count = len(state["text"].split())
    print(f"  [main: count]    {count} words")
    return {"word_count": count}

def summarise(state: PipelineState):
    words = state["text"].split()[:8]
    snippet = " ".join(words) + ("..." if len(state["text"].split()) > 8 else "")
    print(f"  [main: summarise] '{snippet}'")
    return {"summary": f"Text preview: '{snippet}' ({state['word_count']} words)"}

main = StateGraph(PipelineState)
main.add_node("clean",    text_cleaner)   # ← SUBGRAPH as node!
main.add_node("count",    count_words)
main.add_node("summarise",summarise)
main.add_edge(START,      "clean")
main.add_edge("clean",    "count")
main.add_edge("count",    "summarise")
main.add_edge("summarise", END)
pipeline = main.compile()

raw_input = "  Hello, World!   This Is A TEST of SUBGRAPHS.  "
print(f"Input : '{raw_input}'")
print()
result = pipeline.invoke({"text": raw_input, "word_count": 0, "summary": ""})
print()
print(f"Output text : '{result['text']}'")
print(f"Word count  : {result['word_count']}")
print(f"Summary     : {result['summary']}")
print()
print("✅ Subgraph ran as a single node inside the parent pipeline!")
```

sections.title: Example 5 — Validation Subgraph
sections.body:
**A subgraph that validates user input before the main graph processes it.**

```python
# ── SUB-GRAPH: Input Validator ──────────────────────────────────
class ValidationState(TypedDict):
    user_input: str
    is_valid  : bool
    error_msg : str

def check_not_empty(state: ValidationState):
    ok = bool(state["user_input"].strip())
    print(f"  [sub: empty_check] is_valid={ok}")
    return {"is_valid": ok, "error_msg": "" if ok else "Input cannot be empty"}

def check_min_length(state: ValidationState):
    if not state["is_valid"]:
        return {}   # already failed — skip
    ok = len(state["user_input"].strip()) >= 5
    print(f"  [sub: length_check] is_valid={ok}")
    return {"is_valid": ok, "error_msg": "" if ok else "Input too short (min 5 chars)"}

def check_no_spam(state: ValidationState):
    if not state["is_valid"]:
        return {}
    spam_words = ["spam", "buy now", "click here"]
    ok = not any(w in state["user_input"].lower() for w in spam_words)
    print(f"  [sub: spam_check]   is_valid={ok}")
    return {"is_valid": ok, "error_msg": "" if ok else "Spam detected"}

val_sub = StateGraph(ValidationState)
val_sub.add_node("empty",  check_not_empty)
val_sub.add_node("length", check_min_length)
val_sub.add_node("spam",   check_no_spam)
val_sub.add_edge(START,   "empty")
val_sub.add_edge("empty", "length")
val_sub.add_edge("length","spam")
val_sub.add_edge("spam",   END)
validator = val_sub.compile()

# ── PARENT GRAPH ────────────────────────────────────────────────
class FormState(TypedDict):
    user_input: str
    is_valid  : bool
    error_msg : str
    llm_reply : str

def process_valid_input(state: FormState):
    reply = llm.invoke([
        SystemMessage("You are a helpful assistant. Reply in 1 sentence."),
        HumanMessage(state["user_input"])
    ]).content
    return {"llm_reply": reply}

def show_error(state: FormState):
    return {"llm_reply": f"❌ Validation failed: {state['error_msg']}"}

def route_after_validation(state: FormState):
    return "process" if state["is_valid"] else "error"

main = StateGraph(FormState)
main.add_node("validate", validator)        # ← SUBGRAPH as node!
main.add_node("process",  process_valid_input)
main.add_node("error",    show_error)
main.add_edge(START, "validate")
main.add_conditional_edges("validate", route_after_validation, {"process":"process","error":"error"})
main.add_edge("process", END)
main.add_edge("error",   END)
form_app = main.compile()

test_inputs = [
    "Tell me about Python",     # valid
    "hi",                       # too short
    "",                         # empty
    "buy now spam offer",       # spam
]
for user_input in test_inputs:
    r = form_app.invoke({"user_input": user_input, "is_valid": True, "error_msg": "", "llm_reply": ""})
    print(f"Input: '{user_input}' → {r['llm_reply'][:100]}")
    print()
print("✅ Validation subgraph reused across all inputs — modular and clean!")
```

sections.title: Example 6 — LLM Translation Subgraph
sections.body:
**A subgraph that translates text to 3 languages — reused inside a content pipeline.**

```python
# ── SUB-GRAPH: Translator ───────────────────────────────────────
class TranslateState(TypedDict):
    original_text: str
    translations : dict   # {"spanish": "...", "french": "...", "hindi": "..."}

def translate_spanish(state: TranslateState):
    prompt = f"Translate ONLY this text to Spanish (1 sentence): {state['original_text']}"
    result = llm.invoke([HumanMessage(prompt)]).content.strip()
    print(f"  [sub: ES] {result[:60]}")
    existing = dict(state.get("translations") or {})
    existing["spanish"] = result
    return {"translations": existing}

def translate_french(state: TranslateState):
    prompt = f"Translate ONLY this text to French (1 sentence): {state['original_text']}"
    result = llm.invoke([HumanMessage(prompt)]).content.strip()
    print(f"  [sub: FR] {result[:60]}")
    existing = dict(state.get("translations") or {})
    existing["french"] = result
    return {"translations": existing}

def translate_hindi(state: TranslateState):
    prompt = f"Translate ONLY this text to Hindi (1 sentence): {state['original_text']}"
    result = llm.invoke([HumanMessage(prompt)]).content.strip()
    print(f"  [sub: HI] {result[:60]}")
    existing = dict(state.get("translations") or {})
    existing["hindi"] = result
    return {"translations": existing}

trans_sub = StateGraph(TranslateState)
trans_sub.add_node("es", translate_spanish)
trans_sub.add_node("fr", translate_french)
trans_sub.add_node("hi", translate_hindi)
trans_sub.add_edge(START, "es")
trans_sub.add_edge("es",  "fr")
trans_sub.add_edge("fr",  "hi")
trans_sub.add_edge("hi",  END)
translator = trans_sub.compile()

# ── PARENT GRAPH: Content Pipeline ─────────────────────────────
class ContentState(TypedDict):
    original_text: str
    translations : dict
    publish_ready: bool

def mark_ready(state: ContentState):
    is_ready = len(state.get("translations") or {}) == 3
    print(f"  [main: ready_check] all 3 translations done = {is_ready}")
    return {"publish_ready": is_ready}

main = StateGraph(ContentState)
main.add_node("translate", translator)    # ← SUBGRAPH!
main.add_node("ready",     mark_ready)
main.add_edge(START,       "translate")
main.add_edge("translate", "ready")
main.add_edge("ready",     END)
content_app = main.compile()

result = content_app.invoke({
    "original_text": "LangGraph makes building AI agents easy.",
    "translations" : {},
    "publish_ready": False,
})
print()
print("Translations:")
for lang, text in result["translations"].items():
    print(f"  {lang:8s}: {text[:80]}")
print(f"Publish ready: {result['publish_ready']}")
print()
print("✅ Translator subgraph is self-contained and reusable in any pipeline!")
```

sections.title: What is a Multi-Agent System?
sections.body:
Instead of one big graph doing everything, you build a **team of specialist agents**,
each good at one thing, controlled by a **supervisor** that decides who to call.

```
                     ┌─────────────────┐
                     │   SUPERVISOR    │
                     │  (LLM decides   │
                     │   who to call)  │
                     └────────┬────────┘
              ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
              ▼               ▼               ▼
        ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────┐
        │ WRITER   │   │RESEARCHER│   │  CRITIC  │
        │  agent   │   │  agent   │   │  agent   │
        └──────────┘   └──────────┘   └──────────┘
```

### The pattern:
1. Supervisor reads the task and current state
2. Supervisor decides which worker to call next (or "DONE")
3. Chosen worker runs and updates state
4. Loop back to supervisor until task is done

sections.title: Example 7 — Simple Rule-Based Supervisor
sections.body:
**Supervisor without LLM — pure routing logic. Great for understanding the pattern.**

```python
from typing import Literal

WORKERS = ["writer", "editor", "publisher"]

class WorkflowState(TypedDict):
    task    : str
    content : str
    edited  : str
    published: bool
    next_worker: str

def supervisor_node(state: WorkflowState):
    # Simple rule: go through workers in order
    content   = state.get("content", "")
    edited    = state.get("edited",  "")
    published = state.get("published", False)

    if not content:
        next_w = "writer"
    elif not edited:
        next_w = "editor"
    elif not published:
        next_w = "publisher"
    else:
        next_w = "DONE"

    print(f"  [supervisor] → next: {next_w}")
    return {"next_worker": next_w}

def writer_node(state: WorkflowState):
    print(f"  [writer] Writing about: {state['task']}")
    return {"content": f"Draft article about '{state['task']}'. [written]"}

def editor_node(state: WorkflowState):
    print(f"  [editor] Editing the draft...")
    return {"edited": state["content"].replace("[written]", "[edited & polished]")}

def publisher_node(state: WorkflowState):
    print(f"  [publisher] Publishing...")
    return {"published": True}

def route_supervisor(state: WorkflowState) -> str:
    return state["next_worker"]   # route to the chosen worker or END

g = StateGraph(WorkflowState)
g.add_node("supervisor", supervisor_node)
g.add_node("writer",     writer_node)
g.add_node("editor",     editor_node)
g.add_node("publisher",  publisher_node)

g.add_edge(START, "supervisor")
g.add_conditional_edges(
    "supervisor",
    route_supervisor,
    {"writer":"writer","editor":"editor","publisher":"publisher","DONE":END}
)
# Each worker loops back to supervisor
for w in ["writer", "editor", "publisher"]:
    g.add_edge(w, "supervisor")

app = g.compile()
result = app.invoke({
    "task"       : "LangGraph Multi-Agent Systems",
    "content"    : "",
    "edited"     : "",
    "published"  : False,
    "next_worker": "",
})
print()
print(f"Content   : {result['content']}")
print(f"Edited    : {result['edited']}")
print(f"Published : {result['published']}")
print()
print("✅ Supervisor orchestrated 3 workers automatically — looped back each time!")
```

sections.title: Example 8 — LLM Supervisor with Specialist Agents
sections.body:
**The supervisor is an LLM that decides which specialist to call based on the task.**

```python
AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS = {
    "researcher" : "Finds facts and background information on a topic",
    "writer"     : "Writes clear, engaging content based on research",
    "critic"     : "Reviews content and suggests improvements",
}

class AgentState(MessagesState):
    task        : str
    agent_notes : Annotated[dict, lambda old, new: {**old, **new}]
    next_agent  : str
    iteration   : Annotated[int, operator.add]

def llm_supervisor(state: AgentState):
    notes_text = json.dumps(state.get("agent_notes") or {}, indent=2) or "None yet"
    system = SystemMessage(
        "You are a project supervisor managing a team of AI agents.\n"
        f"Task: {state['task']}\n"
        f"Work done so far:\n{notes_text}\n\n"
        "Agents available:\n"
        + "\n".join(f"- {k}: {v}" for k, v in AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS.items()) +
        "\n\nReply with ONLY one word: researcher, writer, critic, or DONE.\n"
        "Say DONE when the task has research + written content + a review."
    )
    choice = llm.invoke([system]).content.strip().lower()
    # Clean up response
    for agent in list(AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS.keys()) + ["done"]:
        if agent in choice:
            choice = agent
            break
    print(f"  [supervisor] iteration {state.get('iteration',0)+1} → {choice}")
    return {"next_agent": choice, "iteration": 1}

def researcher_agent(state: AgentState):
    prompt = [
        SystemMessage("You are a researcher. Provide 2-3 key facts. Be concise."),
        HumanMessage(f"Research: {state['task']}")
    ]
    result = llm.invoke(prompt).content
    print(f"  [researcher] found facts")
    return {"agent_notes": {"research": result[:200]}, "messages": [AIMessage(f"Research: {result[:100]}")]}

def writer_agent(state: AgentState):
    research = state.get("agent_notes", {}).get("research", "No research yet")
    prompt = [
        SystemMessage("You are a writer. Write 2-3 sentences based on the research."),
        HumanMessage(f"Write about: {state['task']}\nResearch: {research}")
    ]
    result = llm.invoke(prompt).content
    print(f"  [writer] wrote content")
    return {"agent_notes": {"draft": result[:200]}, "messages": [AIMessage(f"Draft: {result[:100}")]}

def critic_agent(state: AgentState):
    draft = state.get("agent_notes", {}).get("draft", "No draft yet")
    prompt = [
        SystemMessage("You are a critic. Give ONE improvement suggestion in 1 sentence."),
        HumanMessage(f"Review: {draft}")
    ]
    result = llm.invoke(prompt).content
    print(f"  [critic] gave review")
    return {"agent_notes": {"review": result[:200]}, "messages": [AIMessage(f"Review: {result[:100}")]}

def route_next_agent(state: AgentState) -> str:
    nxt = state.get("next_agent", "DONE")
    if state.get("iteration", 0) >= 5:   # safety limit
        return END
    return nxt if nxt in AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS else END

g = StateGraph(AgentState)
g.add_node("supervisor", llm_supervisor)
g.add_node("researcher", researcher_agent)
g.add_node("writer",     writer_agent)
g.add_node("critic",     critic_agent)
g.add_edge(START, "supervisor")
g.add_conditional_edges("supervisor", route_next_agent,
    {"researcher":"researcher","writer":"writer","critic":"critic",END:END})
for agent in AGENT_DESCRIPTIONS:
    g.add_edge(agent, "supervisor")
app = g.compile()

result = app.invoke({
    "task"       : "Benefits of LangGraph for AI developers",
    "messages"   : [],
    "agent_notes": {},
    "next_agent" : "",
    "iteration"  : 0,
})
print()
print("=== Final Agent Notes ===")
for k, v in result.get("agent_notes", {}).items():
    print(f"[{k}]\n{v[:250]}\n")
print(f"Total iterations: {result['iteration']}")
print("✅ LLM supervisor orchestrated researcher → writer → critic automatically!")
```

sections.title: Example 9 — Parallel Multi-Agent (Fan-out to Agents)
sections.body:
**Launch specialist agents in parallel (fan-out), then a supervisor collects results.**

```python
class ParallelAgentState(TypedDict):
    topic          : str
    sentiment_view : str
    technical_view : str
    business_view  : str
    final_report   : str

# Three specialist agents run in parallel (fan-out)
def sentiment_analyst(state: ParallelAgentState):
    r = llm.invoke([
        SystemMessage("You are a sentiment analyst. 1 sentence only."),
        HumanMessage(f"Sentiment perspective on: {state['topic']}")
    ]).content
    print(f"  [sentiment] done")
    return {"sentiment_view": r}

def technical_analyst(state: ParallelAgentState):
    r = llm.invoke([
        SystemMessage("You are a technical expert. 1 sentence only."),
        HumanMessage(f"Technical perspective on: {state['topic']}")
    ]).content
    print(f"  [technical] done")
    return {"technical_view": r}

def business_analyst(state: ParallelAgentState):
    r = llm.invoke([
        SystemMessage("You are a business strategist. 1 sentence only."),
        HumanMessage(f"Business perspective on: {state['topic']}")
    ]).content
    print(f"  [business] done")
    return {"business_view": r}

# Supervisor collects and synthesises all views
def report_supervisor(state: ParallelAgentState):
    combined = (
        f"Sentiment: {state['sentiment_view']}\n"
        f"Technical: {state['technical_view']}\n"
        f"Business : {state['business_view']}"
    )
    r = llm.invoke([
        SystemMessage("Synthesise these 3 perspectives into ONE paragraph of 3 sentences."),
        HumanMessage(combined)
    ]).content
    print(f"  [supervisor] synthesised all views")
    return {"final_report": r}

g = StateGraph(ParallelAgentState)
g.add_node("sentiment",   sentiment_analyst)
g.add_node("technical",   technical_analyst)
g.add_node("business",    business_analyst)
g.add_node("supervisor",  report_supervisor)

# Fan-out: START triggers all 3 agents simultaneously
g.add_edge(START, "sentiment")
g.add_edge(START, "technical")
g.add_edge(START, "business")

# Fan-in: all 3 converge to supervisor
g.add_edge("sentiment",  "supervisor")
g.add_edge("technical",  "supervisor")
g.add_edge("business",   "supervisor")
g.add_edge("supervisor", END)
app = g.compile()

result = app.invoke({
    "topic"         : "AI Agents replacing human jobs",
    "sentiment_view": "",
    "technical_view": "",
    "business_view" : "",
    "final_report"  : "",
})
print()
print("=== Final Report ===")
print(result["final_report"])
print()
print("✅ 3 agents ran in parallel, supervisor synthesised all views!")
```

sections.title: What is Streaming in LangGraph?
sections.body:
Instead of waiting for the **entire graph to finish**, streaming lets you
see results **as they happen** — node by node, token by token.

```
Without streaming:                 With streaming:
invoke()                           stream()
  │                                  │
  │  ... wait ...                    ├─ node_1 finished → yield state
  │  ... wait ...                    ├─ node_2 finished → yield state
  │  ... wait ...                    ├─ node_3 finished → yield state
  │                                  │
  └─ final result                    └─ done!
```

### Three streaming modes:

| Mode | What you get | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| `"values"` | Full state snapshot after each node | Debugging, progress bars |
| `"updates"` | Only what changed in each node | Efficiency, diffs |
| `"debug"` | Every internal event | Deep debugging |

sections.title: Example 10 — Streaming with mode='values'
sections.body:
**See the complete state snapshot after every single node runs.**

```python
class ProcessState(TypedDict):
    text     : str
    step1_out: str
    step2_out: str
    step3_out: str

def step1(state: ProcessState):
    return {"step1_out": f"[STEP1] Cleaned: '{state['text'].strip()}'"}

def step2(state: ProcessState):
    return {"step2_out": f"[STEP2] Analysed: {len(state['step1_out'])} chars"}

def step3(state: ProcessState):
    return {"step3_out": f"[STEP3] Final: {state['step1_out']} | {state['step2_out']}"}

g = StateGraph(ProcessState)
g.add_node("s1", step1)
g.add_node("s2", step2)
g.add_node("s3", step3)
g.add_edge(START, "s1")
g.add_edge("s1",  "s2")
g.add_edge("s2",  "s3")
g.add_edge("s3",  END)
app = g.compile()

print("=== Streaming mode='values' (full state after each node) ===\n")

for i, snapshot in enumerate(app.stream(
    {"text": "  Hello LangGraph!  ", "step1_out": "", "step2_out": "", "step3_out": ""},
    stream_mode="values"
)):
    print(f"--- Snapshot {i} ---")
    for key, val in snapshot.items():
        if val:   # only print non-empty values
            print(f"  {key}: {val}")
    print()

print("✅ mode='values': you see the ENTIRE state after every node!")
```

sections.title: Example 11 — Streaming with mode='updates'
Example 12 — Streaming LLM Tokens Live
sections.body:
**Stream individual tokens from the LLM as they are generated — essential for chatbots.**

```python
import asyncio

class StreamChatState(MessagesState):
    pass

def stream_bot_node(state: StreamChatState):
    reply = llm.invoke(state["messages"])
    return {"messages": [reply]}

g = StateGraph(StreamChatState)
g.add_node("bot", stream_bot_node)
g.add_edge(START, "bot")
g.add_edge("bot", END)
stream_app = g.compile()

# ── Async streaming of events (including LLM tokens) ──────────
async def stream_tokens(user_message: str):
    print(f"You: {user_message}")
    print("Bot: ", end="", flush=True)

    full_reply = ""
    async for event in stream_app.astream_events(
        {"messages": [HumanMessage(user_message)]},
        version="v2"
    ):
        kind = event["event"]
        # Capture LLM token chunks
        if kind == "on_chat_model_stream":
            chunk = event["data"]["chunk"]
            token = chunk.content
            if token:
                print(token, end="", flush=True)
                full_reply += token

    print()   # newline after streaming
    print(f"\n[Full reply captured: {len(full_reply)} chars]")

# Run the async function
asyncio.run(stream_tokens("Explain LangGraph streaming in one sentence."))
print()
print("✅ astream_events: tokens appear one by one as the LLM generates them!")
```

sections.title: What is Time Travel in LangGraph?
sections.body:
Because every state is saved by the checkpointer after every node,
you can **go back in time** to any point and:
- **Inspect** what the state was
- **Replay** from that point
- **Fork** — change the state and continue differently

```
Thread execution:
  Step 0: state = {count: 0}  ← checkpoint saved
  Step 1: state = {count: 1}  ← checkpoint saved
  Step 2: state = {count: 2}  ← checkpoint saved  ← CURRENT

Time travel:
  Fork from Step 1 → change count to 10 → re-run
  Step 1': state = {count: 10}  ← new branch!
  Step 2': state = {count: 11}
```

### Key APIs:
```python
# List all past states (newest first)
history = list(app.get_state_history(config))

# Get one specific past state
past_state = history[2]
print(past_state.values)          # state values at that point
print(past_state.config)          # config to resume from that point

# Replay from a past checkpoint
app.invoke(None, config=past_state.config)

# Fork: update the past state, then continue
app.update_state(past_state.config, {"count": 99})
app.invoke(None, config=past_state.config)
```

sections.title: Example 13 — Inspecting State History
sections.body:
**Run a graph, then scroll back through every saved checkpoint.**

```python
class CountState(TypedDict):
    count  : int
    history: Annotated[list, operator.add]

def increment(state: CountState):
    new = state.get("count", 0) + 1
    return {"count": new, "history": [f"incremented to {new}"]}

g = StateGraph(CountState)
g.add_node("inc", increment)
g.add_edge(START, "inc")
g.add_edge("inc", END)
app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "time-travel-1"}}

# Run 4 times — each creates a checkpoint
print("Running 4 times...")
for i in range(4):
    r = app.invoke({}, config=cfg)
    print(f"  Run {i+1}: count = {r['count']}")

# Now inspect history
print()
print("=== State History (newest → oldest) ===")
history = list(app.get_state_history(cfg))
print(f"Total checkpoints saved: {len(history)}")
print()
for i, snap in enumerate(history):
    values = snap.values
    print(f"Checkpoint {i}:")
    print(f"  count   = {values.get('count', 0)}")
    print(f"  history = {values.get('history', [])}")
    print(f"  step    = {snap.metadata.get('step', '?')}")
    print()

print("✅ get_state_history: every node execution is checkpointed and browsable!")
```

sections.title: Example 14 — Forking from a Past State
sections.body:
**Change a past state value and re-run from that point — creates a new branch.**

```python
class StoryState(TypedDict):
    chapter : int
    content : Annotated[list, operator.add]

def write_chapter(state: StoryState):
    ch = state.get("chapter", 0) + 1
    text = llm.invoke([
        SystemMessage("You are a story writer. Write ONE sentence for a short story chapter."),
        HumanMessage(f"Write chapter {ch} of a mystery story.")
    ]).content.strip()
    print(f"  Chapter {ch}: {text[:80]}...")
    return {"chapter": ch, "content": [f"Ch{ch}: {text}"]}

g = StateGraph(StoryState)
g.add_node("write", write_chapter)
g.add_edge(START, "write")
g.add_edge("write", END)
app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "story-time-travel"}}

# Write 3 chapters
print("=== Original Timeline ===")
for _ in range(3):
    r = app.invoke({}, config=cfg)

original_chapters = r["content"]
print(f"Original story has {len(original_chapters)} chapters")

# Get history and find chapter 1 checkpoint
history = list(app.get_state_history(cfg))
print(f"\nFound {len(history)} checkpoints")

# Fork from chapter 1 state and inject a different direction
ch1_snap = None
for snap in history:
    if snap.values.get("chapter") == 1:
        ch1_snap = snap
        break

if ch1_snap:
    print(f"\n=== Forking from Chapter 1 ===")
    print(f"Original Chapter 1: {ch1_snap.values['content']}")

    # Update the state at ch1 checkpoint to a different story direction
    fork_config = app.update_state(
        ch1_snap.config,
        {"content": ["Ch1: [FORK] The detective found a hidden door in the library."]}
    )

    # Continue from the fork
    print("\nContinuing from fork...")
    r_fork = app.invoke(None, config=fork_config)
    print(f"Forked story: {r_fork['content']}")
else:
    print("(Could not find chapter 1 checkpoint for demo)")

print()
print("✅ Time travel: forked at chapter 1, continued with a different storyline!")
```

sections.title: Example 15 — Replay for Debugging
sections.body:
**Something went wrong — replay from a known-good checkpoint to debug.**

```python
class CalcState(TypedDict):
    value  : int
    log    : Annotated[list, operator.add]

def double_it(state: CalcState):
    new_val = state.get("value", 1) * 2
    print(f"  [double] {state.get('value',1)} → {new_val}")
    return {"value": new_val, "log": [f"doubled to {new_val}"]}

g = StateGraph(CalcState)
g.add_node("double", double_it)
g.add_edge(START, "double")
g.add_edge("double", END)
app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "debug-replay-1"}}

print("=== Original Run ===")
for i in range(4):
    r = app.invoke({}, config=cfg)
    print(f"  After step {i+1}: value = {r['value']}")

# Something went wrong at step 3 — go back to step 2 state
history = list(app.get_state_history(cfg))
print(f"\nSaved {len(history)} checkpoints")

# Find step 2 (value = 4 = 1*2*2)
step2_snap = None
for snap in history:
    if snap.values.get("value") == 4:
        step2_snap = snap
        break

if step2_snap:
    print(f"\n=== Replaying from step 2 (value=4) ===")
    print(f"State at that point: {step2_snap.values}")
    # Replay from here
    replayed = app.invoke(None, config=step2_snap.config)
    print(f"After replay: value = {replayed['value']}")
    print(f"Log: {replayed['log']}")

print()
print("✅ Time travel replay: jumped back to a known-good state and re-ran!")
```

sections.title: What is create_react_agent?
sections.body:
`create_react_agent` is a **prebuilt function** that creates a full ReAct agent
(Reasoning + Acting) with just ONE line of code.

Instead of manually building the graph with ToolNode, tools_condition, etc.,
you just do:

```python
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent

app = create_react_agent(llm, tools=my_tools)
```

The prebuilt agent handles:
- Calling the LLM with tools bound
- Running the tools when LLM requests them
- Looping back until the LLM gives a final answer (no tool call)

```
START → [agent LLM] → tool call? → [ToolNode] → [agent LLM] → FINAL → END
                    ↓ no tool
                   END
```

> ✨ Use `create_react_agent` for quick prototyping.
> Build manually when you need custom control flow.

sections.title: Example 16 — Basic create_react_agent with Tools
sections.body:
**Build a working ReAct agent in 3 lines — calculator + weather tools.**

```python
# ── Define tools ────────────────────────────────────────────────
@tool
def calculator(expression: str) -> str:
    # Safe calculator: evaluates a math expression string
    try:
        allowed = set("0123456789+-*/()., ")
        if all(c in allowed for c in expression):
            result = eval(expression)
            return f"Result: {result}"
        return "Error: invalid expression"
    except Exception as e:
        return f"Error: {str(e)}"

@tool
def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    # Simulated weather tool
    weather_db = {
        "london"    : "Cloudy, 14°C",
        "new york"  : "Sunny, 22°C",
        "tokyo"     : "Rainy, 18°C",
        "delhi"     : "Hot, 35°C",
        "paris"     : "Partly cloudy, 17°C",
    }
    return weather_db.get(city.lower(), f"Weather data unavailable for {city}")

@tool
def word_count(text: str) -> str:
    # Count words in text
    words = len(text.split())
    chars = len(text)
    return f"Words: {words}, Characters: {chars}"

tools = [calculator, get_weather, word_count]

# ── Create ReAct agent in ONE LINE ──────────────────────────────
agent_app = create_react_agent(llm, tools=tools)

print("=== create_react_agent Demo ===\n")

queries = [
    "What is 25 * 48 + 120?",
    "What's the weather in Tokyo and Paris?",
    "Count the words in: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
]

for query in queries:
    print(f"❓ {query}")
    result = agent_app.invoke({"messages": [HumanMessage(query)]})
    final_msg = result["messages"][-1].content
    print(f"✅ {final_msg[:200]}")
    print()
print("✅ create_react_agent: full ReAct agent with tools in 1 line!")
```

sections.title: What is the Send API?
sections.body:
The `Send` API lets you **dynamically create parallel executions** at runtime.

Instead of having a fixed number of parallel nodes, you can:
- Take a list of items from state
- Send each item to the same node in parallel
- All run simultaneously, then results merge back

```
                ┌─────────────────────┐
                │    fan_out_node     │
                │  returns [Send(...),│
                │   Send(...),        │
                │    Send(...)]       │
                └──────┬──────┬───┘
                       │      │      │
                   Send-1  Send-2  Send-3
                       │      │      │
                ┌──────▼──────▼──────▼──┐
                │     process_node      │
                │  (runs 3 times in     │
                │   parallel)           │
                └───────────┬───────────┘
                            │
                       final_node
```

This is also called the **Map-Reduce** pattern:
- **Map**: fan out with Send (process each item)
- **Reduce**: gather node collects all results

sections.title: Example 19 — Dynamic Fan-out with Send
sections.body:
**Process a variable-length list of items in parallel — each gets its own Send.**

```python
class ItemState(TypedDict):
    item   : str
    result : str

class MapReduceState(TypedDict):
    items  : List[str]
    results: Annotated[list, operator.add]   # ← reducer collects all results
    summary: str

# ── Process one item (called N times in parallel via Send) ──────
def process_item(state: ItemState):
    item = state["item"]
    processed = f"[PROCESSED] {item.upper()} ({len(item)} chars)"
    print(f"  processing: '{item}' → '{processed}'")
    return {"result": processed}

# ── Fan-out: returns a Send for each item ──────────────────────
def fan_out(state: MapReduceState):
    print(f"  fan_out: creating {len(state['items'])} parallel tasks")
    return [Send("process_item", {"item": item, "result": ""}) for item in state["items"]]

# ── Collect node: gathers Send results back to MapReduceState ──
# Note: Send's results go into 'results' via the reducer
def collect_results(state: MapReduceState):
    print(f"  collect: received {len(state['results'])} results")
    summary = " | ".join(state["results"])
    return {"summary": f"Processed {len(state['results'])} items: {summary}"}

g = StateGraph(MapReduceState)
g.add_node("process_item",  process_item)
g.add_node("collect",       collect_results)

# fan_out returns a list of Send objects → conditional_edges handles it
g.add_conditional_edges(START, fan_out, ["process_item"])
g.add_edge("process_item",  "collect")   # each parallel task goes to collect
g.add_edge("collect",       END)
app = g.compile()

# Dynamic list — can be any length!
my_items = ["banana", "apple", "cherry", "elderberry", "fig"]
print(f"=== Processing {len(my_items)} items in parallel ===\n")

result = app.invoke({
    "items"  : my_items,
    "results": [],
    "summary": "",
})
print()
print(f"Summary: {result['summary']}")
print()
print("✅ Send API: each item processed in its own parallel execution!")
```

sections.title: Example 20 — Map-Reduce with LLM (Parallel Document Analysis)
sections.body:
**Analyse multiple documents in parallel using Send, then reduce to one report.**

```python
DOCUMENTS = [
    "Python was created by Guido van Rossum in 1991. It emphasizes code readability.",
    "LangGraph is a library for building stateful multi-agent systems using LLM.",
    "SQLite is a lightweight embedded database used in millions of applications.",
    "Docker is a platform for containerizing applications for consistent deployment.",
]

class DocState(TypedDict):
    doc_id  : int
    document: str
    analysis: str   # LLM analysis of one document

class ReportState(TypedDict):
    documents: List[str]
    analyses : Annotated[list, operator.add]   # reducer collects all LLM analyses
    report   : str

def analyse_doc(state: DocState):
    prompt = [
        SystemMessage("Summarise this text in ONE sentence. Be concise."),
        HumanMessage(state["document"])
    ]
    analysis = llm.invoke(prompt).content.strip()
    print(f"  [doc {state['doc_id']}] analysed: {analysis[:60]}...")
    return {"analysis": f"Doc {state['doc_id']}: {analysis}"}

def fan_out_docs(state: ReportState):
    print(f"  fan_out: sending {len(state['documents'])} docs to LLM in parallel")
    return [
        Send("analyse_doc", {"doc_id": i, "document": doc, "analysis": ""})
        for i, doc in enumerate(state["documents"])
    ]

def generate_report(state: ReportState):
    analyses_text = "\n".join(state["analyses"])
    report = llm.invoke([
        SystemMessage("You are a report writer. Write a 2-sentence executive summary."),
        HumanMessage(f"Individual document analyses:\n{analyses_text}")
    ]).content.strip()
    print(f"  [report] generated")
    return {"report": report}

g = StateGraph(ReportState)
g.add_node("analyse_doc",     analyse_doc)
g.add_node("generate_report", generate_report)
g.add_conditional_edges(START, fan_out_docs, ["analyse_doc"])
g.add_edge("analyse_doc",     "generate_report")
g.add_edge("generate_report", END)
app = g.compile()

print(f"=== Parallel Document Analysis ({len(DOCUMENTS)} docs) ===\n")
result = app.invoke({"documents": DOCUMENTS, "analyses": [], "report": ""})

print()
print("=== Individual Analyses ===")
for a in result["analyses"]:
    print(f"  {a}")

print()
print("=== Executive Report ===")
print(result["report"])
print()
print("✅ Send API map-reduce: all docs analysed in parallel, one report generated!")
```

sections.title: Example 21 — Send API with Batching
sections.body:
**Dynamic batch processing — split a large dataset into chunks and process in parallel.**

```python
import math

class BatchState(TypedDict):
    batch_id : int
    items    : List[int]
    batch_sum: int

class BatchJobState(TypedDict):
    all_numbers : List[int]
    batch_sums  : Annotated[list, operator.add]
    total       : int
    batch_size  : int

def process_batch(state: BatchState):
    total = sum(state["items"])
    print(f"  [batch {state['batch_id']}] items={state['items']} sum={total}")
    return {"batch_sum": total}

def create_batches(state: BatchJobState):
    numbers    = state["all_numbers"]
    batch_size = state.get("batch_size", 3)
    n_batches  = math.ceil(len(numbers) / batch_size)
    print(f"  fan_out: {len(numbers)} numbers → {n_batches} batches of size {batch_size}")
    sends = []
    for i in range(n_batches):
        chunk = numbers[i * batch_size : (i + 1) * batch_size]
        sends.append(Send("process_batch", {"batch_id": i, "items": chunk, "batch_sum": 0}))
    return sends

def aggregate(state: BatchJobState):
    total = sum(state["batch_sums"])
    print(f"  [aggregate] batch sums={state['batch_sums']} total={total}")
    return {"total": total}

g = StateGraph(BatchJobState)
g.add_node("process_batch", process_batch)
g.add_node("aggregate",     aggregate)
g.add_conditional_edges(START, create_batches, ["process_batch"])
g.add_edge("process_batch", "aggregate")
g.add_edge("aggregate",     END)
app = g.compile()

numbers = list(range(1, 13))   # 1 to 12
print(f"=== Batch Processing: sum of {numbers} ===\n")

result = app.invoke({
    "all_numbers": numbers,
    "batch_sums" : [],
    "total"      : 0,
    "batch_size" : 4,
})
print()
print(f"Numbers   : {numbers}")
print(f"Batch sums: {result['batch_sums']}")
print(f"Total     : {result['total']}  (expected: {sum(numbers)})")
print()
print("✅ Send API batching: any-sized dataset split into parallel batches dynamically!")
```

sections.title: Quick Reference: When to Use What
sections.body:
| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Simple chatbot state | `MessagesState` |
| Modular/reusable pipeline step | **Subgraph** |
| Multiple specialist AI agents | **Supervisor pattern** |
| See output live / stream tokens | **`.stream()` / `astream_events()`** |
| Debug by going back in time | **Time travel + `get_state_history()`** |
| Quick ReAct agent with tools | **`create_react_agent`** |
| Process a variable-length list in parallel | **Send API** |
| Map data → process → reduce to one result | **Send API map-reduce** |

sections.title: The Complete LangGraph Pattern Cheat Sheet
sections.body:
```python
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, MessagesState, START, END
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent, ToolNode, tools_condition
from langgraph.types import Send, interrupt, Command
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver

# 1. MessagesState
class MyState(MessagesState): extra_field: str

# 2. Subgraph
sub_app = sub_graph.compile()
main.add_node("sub_node", sub_app)

# 3. Supervisor
def supervisor(state): ...    # LLM decides next worker
main.add_conditional_edges("supervisor", route_fn, {worker: worker, "DONE": END})

# 4. Streaming
for snapshot in app.stream(input, stream_mode="values"): ...
for update in app.stream(input, stream_mode="updates"): ...
async for event in app.astream_events(input, version="v2"): ...

# 5. Time Travel
history = list(app.get_state_history(config))
app.invoke(None, config=history[2].config)   # replay
app.update_state(history[2].config, new_values)  # fork

# 6. create_react_agent
agent = create_react_agent(llm, tools=my_tools, checkpointer=MemorySaver())

# 7. Send API
def fan_out(state): return [Send("node", {"item": x}) for x in state["items"]]
graph.add_conditional_edges(START, fan_out, ["node"])
```
